correctness.rationale: For standard H=3/4 fBm and independent Gaussian noise, Gaussian projection gives Var(J)=2/7 and information c(t)^2/(t^(3/2)+η), where c(t)=Cov(J,B_t). An independent global check at η=1/2: set g=2c and d=1−t^(3/2). Integration of g′ gives g=1−d/3−e, where e is the integral from t to 1 of (1−s)s^(1/2)+(1−s)^(3/2). Since 1−s≥(2/3)(1−s^(3/2)), e≥2d²/9. The difference 1−d/3−sqrt(1−2d/3) is (d²/9)/(1−d/3+sqrt(1−2d/3))≤d²/6. Thus 0≤g<sqrt(1−2d/3) for t<1, proving strict terminal superiority including at the threshold. Comparing cross-multiplied informations, the endpoint advantage increases with η since c(t)<c(1)=1/2. The endpoint derivative of information has sign η−1/2; below the threshold continuity, including the zero-information limit at t=0 even without noise, gives an interior maximizer. The terminal risk and the general-H necessary condition follow by substitution and differentiation; no interior uniqueness or general-H sufficiency is shown.
